## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 6.2.2) is a subsection of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Structurally, the chapters of the *Yamaka* regularly divide their procedural or process sections (*pavattivāra*) into three operational modes: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and combined origination-and-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. Through a rigorous matrix of paired questions and categorical distributions, the *nirodhavāra* investigates the temporal dynamics of how particular phenomena cease in relation to persons and realms [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. Scholarly analysis observes that this formal examination reflects an early Buddhist process metaphysics and marks a critical milestone in the development of the Abhidhamma theory of momentariness, utilizing the technical division of a moment (*khaṇa*) into phases of origination and dissolution (*uppādakkhaṇa*, *bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005].
Secondary literature rarely treats Ya 6.2.2 in isolation; references to the title *nirodhavāra* in academic and doctrinal treatises predominantly refer either to the cessation sequence of dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) or to the broader procedural framework shared across the *Yamaka* chapters [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. SuttaCentral registers one modern translation of this section [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse data generated by DharmaNexus highlights the highly formulaic and repetitive composition of the *Yamaka*, recording 11,504 matching passages between this text and 45 other Pāli works [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal alignments are with immediately neighboring sections of the same chapter—namely *Uppādavāra* (Ya 6.2.1) and *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 6.2.3)—as well as corresponding *nirodhavāra* treatments across other *Yamaka* books, such as Ya 3.2.2, Ya 9.2.2, Ya 5.2.2, and Ya 2.2.2 [DharmaNexus]. No curated cross-canonical parallels are identified on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral], but DharmaNexus detects machine-generated thematic alignments with Northern Buddhist scholastic treatises, including the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā-lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093) and Sthiramati's Sanskrit *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā* [DharmaNexus].
